bugs.creator: jeroenooms
bugs.summary: as.POSIXct() gives NA for years where tm_year + 1900 overflows int (OpenBSD mktime)

comments.text:
Created attachment 4080
Fix mktime overflow in OpenBSD

On OpenBSD, tests/datetime3.R fails in the PR#19038 test:

  > x <- as.POSIXlt(c("1900-01-01", "1900-01-01"), tz="UTC")
  > x$year <- .Machine$integer.max - (1901:1899)
  > diff(as.vector(as.POSIXct(x, tz="Etc/UTC")))
  [1] 31536000       NA          # tz="UTC" gives 31536000 31536000

For time zones other than UTC, mktime0() in src/main/datetime.c calls
the system mktime() when configure found it to work for all years.
OpenBSD's mktime() (lib/libc/time/localtime.c, time2sub()) converts
tm_year to a calendar year with increment_overflow32(&y, TM_YEAR_BASE),
so it returns -1 when tm_year + 1900 > INT_MAX, even though the result
fits in a 64-bit time_t. glibc and FreeBSD handle this.

The attached patch uses R's existing extrapolation (guess_offset() +
timegm00()) for those years, as mktime0() already does for years where
mktime() is not trusted. Years up to INT_MAX - 1900 are unaffected. On
glibc, results for six time zones at these years are unchanged, except
Lord Howe in July, where glibc's mktime() gave UTC+10:00 and the patch
gives the zone's standard time UTC+10:30.

comments.text: I found this bug can be worked around by building R with `--with-internal-tzcode` but as this is not the default fixing it would still be preferable.
